questions.question: Which example is representational rather than allocational harm?
options: A hiring classifier gives one group fewer interview invitations
A credit model assigns different loan limits at the same repayment risk
A generated portrayal repeatedly depicts nurses as exclusively female
A benefits system delays one group's payments
questions.explanation: Representational harm concerns stereotypes, erasure, or demeaning portrayal; the nurse example changes how a group is depicted. Allocational harm changes access to material opportunities or resources.

questions.question: How does the toy compute its WEAT-shaped effect size?
options: It counts only exact occurrences of identity words in the output
It computes demographic parity from classifier predictions
It uses the model's perplexity on a single sentence
It compares mean cosine association with X versus Y for identity group A and subtracts the corresponding value for B
questions.explanation: weat_score computes s(w)=mean cos(w,X)-mean cos(w,Y), averages s over A and B, and returns mean_A - mean_B. The result is an embedding association, not an allocation metric.

questions.question: What does debias do to the toy attribute embeddings?
options: It projects the engineer/care attribute vectors away from the gender direction [1,-1,0,0]
It deletes the identity words from EMB
It changes the WEAT formula to use Euclidean distance
It retrains a language model with balanced labels
questions.explanation: debias computes the projection of each attribute vector on gender_dir and subtracts it. Identity vectors remain fixed, so the post-debias score measures a partial reduction rather than a new embedding model.

questions.question: The demo changes the WEAT effect size from +0.8906 to +0.2212. What is the safe interpretation?
options: All behavioural bias has been eliminated
The projection reduced the measured embedding association but does not establish fairness in generated text or decisions
The metric was not computed before debiasing
The positive sign proves group B is more associated with technical terms after debiasing
questions.explanation: The reduction is evidence about this four-dimensional embedding and this WEAT comparison. The lesson explicitly requires probability- and generated-text-based tests for residual behavioural bias.

questions.question: Which three metric families does Gallegos et al. use to organize bias evaluation?
options: Input, output, and custom moderation layers
Pre-training, PPO, and DPO losses
Embedding-based, probability-based, and generated-text-based measures
Accuracy, latency, and memory only
questions.explanation: Embedding tests expose associations, probability tests expose stereotyped likelihoods, and generated-text tests measure downstream behaviour. No one family covers representational and allocational harms by itself.

questions.question: Why is intersectional evaluation needed in addition to single-axis checks?
options: It is only a cheaper form of cross-validation
It guarantees demographic parity for every subgroup
It avoids choosing any fairness definition
A pattern at a gender-by-race intersection can disappear when gender and race are averaged separately
questions.explanation: Intersectional groups can experience a distinct error or portrayal pattern that neither marginal analysis reveals. The lesson's Black-women/Black-men example motivates reporting subgroup slices rather than relying on one aggregate.
